decision: Which approach best resolves: WF-100 creates a renewal quote from a contract and auto-creates the renewal deal. The acceptance signal that turns the quote into a new contract is NOT sourced in the research. Where does that signal come from in the data model?

state.problem: WF-100 creates a renewal quote from a contract and auto-creates the renewal deal. The acceptance signal that turns the quote into a new contract is NOT sourced in the research. Where does that signal come from in the data model?

candidate_solutions.explicit_room_action: The room owns the acceptance. A POST /quotes/{id}/accept route records the acceptance and, in the same call, creates the new contract, links it to the prior contract as a renewal chain and creates the deal. Nothing is inferred. Cost: the buyer-facing accept click is not modelled as a separate actor.
candidate_solutions.inferred_from_status_field: A quote carries a status. PATCH /quotes/{id}/status to 'accepted' triggers the contract creation as a side effect of the status write. Cost: a status write has a hidden side effect that creates two records, so a caller cannot change the status without creating a contract.
candidate_solutions.separate_finalize_step: Acceptance and finalization are two steps. POST /renewal-quotes/{id}/accept only marks the quote accepted. A second call finalizes and creates the contract and deal. Cost: a half-finished renewal is a state a reviewer must reason about, and the spec says acceptance alone creates the contract.

context.evidence: The spec says 'When a renewal quote is accepted, a new contract is created and automatically associated with the previous contract.' It never says who accepts or how the room learns that it happened.
context.product_rule: Every write goes through AuditedDatabase and its audit row names a route the app actually serves.

decision: Which approach best resolves: WF-100 ships with three facts the research does not state: the acceptance signal, the draft and shared quote states, and the Re-enroll behaviour. This build records all three as decisions rather than sourcing them. Is that the right handling?

state.problem: WF-100 ships with three facts the research does not state: the acceptance signal, the draft and shared quote states, and the Re-enroll behaviour. This build records all three as decisions rather than sourcing them. Is that the right handling?

candidate_solutions.record_the_derivation: Keep the current handling. Every unsourced fact is served at GET /decisions with what was chosen, what was rejected, what the choice cost and a sourced flag. The frontend repeats each one on the page and stamps acceptance_signal_sourced: false on every created contract. A reviewer can see exactly which statements are evidence and which are judgement. Cost: three states in the state machine have no citation, so a later audit cannot point at a source for them.
candidate_solutions.narrow_the_surface_to_sourced_behaviour: Drop every unsourced element. Remove the draft and shared states and keep only created and accepted. Refuse to implement Re-enroll. Accept through an explicit action with no commentary. Cost: a seller cannot mark a quote as sent, so the workflow loses the step the researched user flow describes between creating a quote and the buyer accepting it. Re-enroll becomes a field the room ignores, which is the one behaviour a reviewer cannot check.
candidate_solutions.block_until_a_human_sources_them: Refuse to merge and ask a human for the missing research. Cost: the researched transition, the one thing the issue is built around, is already sourced and already implemented. The three open items are secondary. Blocking here ships nothing and the browser verification and reviewer bot never run.

context.acceptance_signal: The research says 'When a renewal quote is accepted, a new contract is created and automatically associated with the previous contract.' It never says who accepts or how the room learns it happened. Choosing an explicit room action over inferring acceptance from a status write passed Jev at 0.91 in audit jev-20261004T231639-22752-99672.
context.quote_states: draft, shared, accepted and superseded. The research names the entry point and accepted. The middle two are this build's choice and DERIVED_NOT_SOURCED says so in the vocabulary, in the quotes listing and on the page.
context.re_enroll: The research names a Re-enroll switch and never describes it. Both behaviours are implemented, so a reviewer can see which one moves and which one does not.
context.direct_renewal: The BETA bypass is recorded as not built and served at GET /vocabulary. It is not one of the three above.
